questions.q: Decimal value of $(101101)_{2}$?
Which of these cannot be a valid octal number?
Decimal value of $(FF)_{16}$?
Decimal value of 4-bit 2's complement $(1011)_{2}$?
Range of 8-bit 2's complement numbers?
Minimum number of 2-input NAND gates to build a 4-input NAND gate?
For $F=\sum(0,1,3,4,6)$ on a 4-to-1 MUX with $S_{1}=B, S_{0}=C$, $D_{0}$ (for $BC=00$) equals?
exp: Both are in the set ($0$ and $4$): $D_{0}=1$.

questions.q: Full adder with $A=1, B=1, C_{in}=0$. Sum $S$?
exp: Two ones is even parity; carry-out is $1$.

questions.q: De Morgan: $\overline{A \cdot B}$ equals?
exp: Break the bar, flip AND to OR.

questions.q: NOR SR latch with $S=1, R=1$?
exp: Both NOR outputs forced $0$, so $Q=\bar{Q}=0$ (not complements).
Releasing both together races — never assert both.

questions.q: JK flip-flop with $J=K=1$?
exp: Toggles each clock — this fixes the SR forbidden state.

questions.q: Number of states of a 4-flip-flop Johnson counter?
States in a non-overlapping Moore FSM detecting the $1011$ pattern?
exp: Moore needs a distinct output state: $S_{0}$ idle, $S_{1}$ got $1$, $S_{2}$ got $10$, $S_{3}$ got $101$, $S_{4}$ got $1011$ with $Z=1$.
Five states; Mealy would need four.

questions.q: Setup time means data must be stable…?
exp: Setup guards sampling: $D$ must be ready BEFORE the edge.
Hold keeps $D$ stable AFTER the edge.

questions.q: Series RC circuit: $V_{R}=12V$ RMS, $V_{C}=15V$ RMS. Source voltage?
exp: Resistor and capacitor voltages are $90^{\circ}$ apart — add by Pythagoras, not directly.

questions.q: A $6kHz$ sinusoidal voltage drives a series RC circuit. Frequency of the voltage across the resistor?
exp: R, L, C are linear: they change amplitude/phase only.
No new frequencies are created — output stays $6kHz$.

questions.q: To realise impedance $1+4j\,\Omega$ at $\omega=1$ rad/s, the real part needs?
exp: Real part $1$ is an ordinary resistance.

questions.q: To realise $+j4$ at $\omega=1$ rad/s (series), use?
exp: $j \times 1 \times L = j4$ gives $L = 4H$. A capacitor would give $-j$.

questions.q: For $R=1k\Omega, C=1\mu F$, the time constant $\tau$?
90 applied; 10 had neither sales nor publishing experience; 65 sales; 58 publishing. Both?
Worker A needs 6 days, B needs 12 days. Together?
Ram is Rs 2 short of a book's price, Shyam Rs 24 short; pooled money still short. Price (integer Rs)?
Train at $15$ m/s passes a man in $20s$ and a station in $36s$. Platform length?
If $x$ is $80\%$ of $y$, then $y$ is what percent of $2x$?
exp: Base is $2x$: $1.25/2 = 0.625 = 62.5\%$. Underline the OF base.

questions.q: Price rises $20\%$, then falls $20\%$. Net change?
LCM of $4$ and $6$?
Two fair coins tossed. P(at least one head)?
Angle between clock hands at 3:00?

sections.title: Section A — Fill in the blanks

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: Minimum number of 2-input NAND gates needed to realise a 4-input NAND gate: ___
exp: Cascade: NAND(A,B), invert to AB, NAND(AB,C), invert to ABC, NAND(ABC,D) — five gates.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: A 3-to-8 decoder has ___ output lines.
exp: An n-to-2^n decoder has 2^n outputs; 2^3 = 8, one per minterm.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: A MOD-10 (decade) counter needs ___ flip-flops.
exp: 2^3 = 8 < 10 ≤ 16 = 2^4, so 4 flip-flops with reset decoded at 1010.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: For R = 1kΩ and C = 1µF, the time constant τ = ___ ms.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: Series RC: VR = 12V RMS, VC = 15V RMS. Source Vs ≈ ___ V RMS.
exp: Vs = √(12² + 15²) = √369 ≈ 19.2V. Adding 12 + 15 = 27V is the trap — quadrature adds by squares.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Memory used by a variable of type short int is ___ bytes (typical x86-64 Linux).
exp: short is 16-bit on the assumed platform: 2 bytes.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: In C, the integer literal 010 equals ___ in decimal.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: The operator group with the highest precedence in C is ___ (postfix / () / []).
exp: Postfix () [] . -> ++ -- binds tightest; comma is loosest.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: LCM of 4 and 6 is ___.
exp: First common multiple of 4 and 6 is 12.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: An ordinary (non-leap) year has ___ odd day(s).
exp: 365 = 52×7 + 1: one odd day. A leap year has 2.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: State De Morgan's theorems for two variables.
questions.model: NEG(A+B) = NEG(A)·NEG(B) and NEG(A·B) = NEG(A)+NEG(B). Break the bar, flip AND/OR.
exp: De Morgan converts AND-OR networks to NAND-NAND for CMOS and drives every NAND-only design.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: Write the sum and carry equations of a half adder.
questions.model: S = A XOR B; C = A·B. Sum is 1 when inputs differ; carry is 1 only when both are 1.
exp: S = odd parity, C = AND. A full adder adds Cin: S = A⊕B⊕Cin.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: Distinguish Moore and Mealy machine outputs in one line each.
questions.model: Moore: output Z = f(state) only — written inside the state circle, changes on clock edges. Mealy: output Z = f(state, input) — written on transition arcs, reacts within the cycle.
exp: Moore costs an extra state but is glitch-free; Mealy is compact (1011 in 4 states vs 5) but can glitch.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: State Kirchhoff's current law and voltage law in one line each.
questions.model: KCL: algebraic sum of currents at a node is zero (in = out). KVL: algebraic sum of voltages around any closed loop is zero (rises = drops).
exp: KCL feeds nodal analysis; KVL feeds mesh analysis.

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: State the maximum power transfer condition and the Pmax formula.
questions.model: Load receives maximum power when RL = Rth. Pmax = Vth²/(4·Rth), at 50% efficiency.
exp: Used for signal matching, never for power grids (efficiency is only 50%).

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: What happens when break is missing in a switch case? Give a one-line example.
questions.model: Execution falls through into the next case. switch(2){case 1:printf("A");case 2:printf("B");case 3:printf("C");} prints BC.
exp: Trace downward from the matched label, collecting every case body until break or end.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: How are arguments passed to functions in C? What does this imply for swap(a,b) with plain ints?
questions.model: By value — the callee gets copies. Plain swap(a,b) swaps only copies, so caller variables are unchanged; pass &a,&b (pointers) to swap for real.
exp: Arrays decay to pointers, so array arguments CAN be modified by the callee.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: What is argv[0]? For the command `prog 10 hi`, give argc and argv[1].
questions.model: argv[0] is the program name. prog 10 hi: argc = 3, argv[1] = "10" (a string, convert with atoi/strtol for numbers).
exp: User arguments start at argv[1]; needing N args means argc == N+1.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: x is 80% of y. What percent of x is y?
exp: Base flip: percent OF x, not of y. Convert 0.8 = 4/5 early.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A finishes a job in 10 days, B in 15 days. Working together, how long?
questions.model: 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6 per day. Together: 6 days (pair formula ab/(a+b) = 150/25).
exp: Never average the days — add reciprocals, invert at the end.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: P(6) on a fair die? P(red card) from a 52-card deck?
questions.model: P(6) = 1/6 (one of six faces). P(red) = 26/52 = 1/2.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Write the clock angle formula and give the number of odd days in a leap year.
questions.model: Angle = |30H − 5.5M| (take min with 360). A leap year has 2 odd days (366 = 52×7 + 2).

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: Implement F(A,B,C) = Σ(0,1,3,4,6) using only a single 4-to-1 multiplexer with B,C as select lines. Give D0..D3 and verify one 1-row and one 0-row.
questions.model: Rows per BC: BC=00 → m0=1,m4=1 ⇒ D0=1. BC=01 → m1=1,m5=0 ⇒ D1=Ā. BC=10 → m2=0,m6=1 ⇒ D2=A. BC=11 → m3=1,m7=0 ⇒ D3=Ā. Wire S1=B,S0=C. Verify ABC=011: selects 11 → D3=Ā=1 ✓ (m3=1). Verify ABC=101: selects 01 → D1=Ā=0 ✓ (m5=0).
exp: Rule per select combo: both rows 0 → tie 0; both 1 → tie 1; only A=0 row is 1 → Ā; only A=1 row is 1 → A.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: Add 0111 (+7) and 0001 (+1) in 4-bit 2's complement. Give the 4-bit result, its decoded value, and say whether overflow occurred with reason.
questions.model: 0111 + 0001 = 1000. Decoded: MSB 1 → negative; invert 0111, +1 → 1000 = 8, so −8. Positive + positive gave negative — impossible, hence overflow. True sum 8 exceeds max +7; needs 5 bits.
exp: Overflow = carry into sign XOR carry out; equivalently an impossible sign. Discarded final carry alone is normal, not overflow.

questions.subject: Digital Design
questions.q: For the synchronous non-overlapping Moore FSM detecting 1011: how many states, and what are the transitions out of the final state S4?
questions.model: 5 states (S0 idle, S1 got 1, S2 got 10, S3 got 101, S4 got 1011 with Z=1). Non-overlapping restart: S4,0→S0 and S4,1→S1.
exp: Overlapping variant would reuse the tail: S4,0→S2, S4,1→S1. VEDA asks non-overlapping (restart).

questions.subject: Basic Electronics
questions.q: R = 1kΩ, C = 1µF, input is a 200 Hz square wave into a series-C (high-pass) RC circuit. Compute τ and the half-period, name the regime, and describe the Vout shape.
questions.model: τ = RC = 1 ms. T = 1/200 = 5 ms, half-period 2.5 ms = 2.5τ — transitional regime. Vout: tilted square with exponential sag toward 0 V between edges (capacitor voltage continuous, cannot jump); visible rounding/tilt, not sharp spikes (those need T/2 ≪ τ) and not a clean square (needs T/2 ≫ τ).
exp: Compare T/2 with τ first: >5τ square-ish, <0.2τ spikes/ramps, between → exponential tilt.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Write a C program to read one input character and print whether it is a digit, a lowercase letter, an uppercase letter, or a special character.
scheme: 1M reading the char (int c for EOF)

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: Predict the output of: switch(2){case 1:printf("A");case 2:printf("B");case 3:printf("C");} Explain in one line.
questions.model: Output BC. case 2 matches and prints B; with no break, execution falls through into case 3 and prints C.
exp: Missing break slides into the next case body, including default.

questions.subject: C Programming
questions.q: With #define SQ(x) ((x)*(x)), what is SQ(2+1)? What would it be with #define SQ(x) x*x? State the macro rule.
questions.model: ((2+1)*(2+1)) = 9 with the parenthesised macro. Bare x*x expands to 2+1*2+1 = 5. Rule: parenthesise the macro body and every parameter use; never pass side effects (SQ(i++) would increment twice).
exp: Macros are text substitution before compiling — no type checks, re-evaluated args.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: 90 people applied for a salesperson job at a book publisher. 10 had neither sales nor publishing background; 65 had sales experience; 58 had publishing background. How many had both? Show steps.
questions.model: Inside the circles: 90 − 10 = 80. Overlap counted twice: 65 + 58 − 80 = 43. Answer 43.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: A train at 15 m/s passes a man on a platform in 20 s and the whole station in 36 s. Find the platform length.
questions.model: Train length = 15×20 = 300 m. Train + platform = 15×36 = 540 m. Platform = 540 − 300 = 240 m.
exp: Point object: own length only. Extended object: add lengths.

questions.subject: Aptitude
questions.q: Ram is Rs 2 short of a book's price and Shyam Rs 24 short; even together they cannot buy it. Find the integer-rupee price.
questions.model: Ram has P−2, Shyam P−24 (both ≥ 0, so P > 24). Together short: (P−2)+(P−24) < P ⇒ P < 26. Integer P with 24 < P < 26: Rs 25.
exp: Bounds squeeze to a single integer — verify positivity too.
